title: Asia Rallies on Chip Stocks and Europe Firms as US Bonds Sit Out Veterans Day
dek: Seoul and Tokyo led Asian gains after Tuesday's hot CPI selloff, Nasdaq futures pointed to a rebound, and the 10-year Treasury's 4.98% close left the market without a fresh bond signal.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Black-and-white photograph of an automatic ticker apparatus on the New York Stock Exchange trading floor
image.credit: Library of Congress via Wikimedia Commons

keyPoints: Seoul's Kospi closed up 2.6% at 5,375.36, rising 136.23 points, with chip stocks leading (Yonhap News Agency, Nov. 11 close).
Tokyo's Nikkei 225 rose about 1.3% to 61,248.52 in the Asian session, according to TradingKey; one early report had shown a small decline, so treat the exact move as provisional.
US stock futures were firmer: S&P 500 futures rose about 0.9% and Nasdaq futures were pointing to a rebound, per investingLive's European wrap published 12:44 PM on Nov. 11.
The US bond market is closed for Veterans Day. SIFMA recommended a full close for dollar fixed income on Nov. 11, so there is no cash Treasury price to guide the session.
body:
Asian equities recovered on Wednesday after Tuesday's selloff in US stocks, which followed a hotter-than-expected October consumer price report. The move was led by chipmakers, which had been the weakest group on Wall Street a day earlier.

## Asia: chips carry the rebound

South Korea's Kospi closed up 2.6% at 5,375.36, according to Yonhap News Agency's close report, with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix higher. Japan's Nikkei 225 gained about 1.3% to 61,248.52 in the reading reported by TradingKey. Other early reports had shown a smaller or negative Nikkei move, so that figure should be treated as provisional until a final exchange close is confirmed.

The chip rebound matters for the wider market because Nvidia's slide on Tuesday was the main drag on the Nasdaq Composite, which fell 0.74%. A steadier semiconductor tape overnight is the first sign that the selling may be easing.

## Europe and futures: firmer tone, thin liquidity

European stocks were higher in the morning session. investingLive reported that the DAX was approaching fresh record highs, and that S&P 500 futures were up about 0.9% by midday in Europe on Nov. 11. Nasdaq futures were pointing to a stronger open after CoreWeave's earnings report on Tuesday, which investingLive linked to a better AI outlook.

Trading conditions were thinner than usual. The US bond market was closed, and fewer participants were active in Europe, which can exaggerate moves in either direction.

## Yields and the Fed: the last clean read is Tuesday

The last cash Treasury reading was Tuesday's close. CNN reported that the 10-year yield rose 10 basis points to 4.98% and briefly traded above 5%, while the two-year yield jumped about 17 basis points. Fed Governor Chris Waller said he would consider a half-point hike at the December meeting if core inflation keeps printing at 0.3% or higher. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said the Fed may need to move faster this winter.

CME FedWatch odds, as reported by CNN for Tuesday, put a quarter-point December hike at 91% and a half-point move at 9%. CNBC, cited in our earlier coverage, put the half-point odds at about 13.6%. The two reports used different snapshots, so the exact figure is not settled; both point to a December hike as the base case.

## Dollar and oil

investingLive reported USD/JPY near 159.00, its highest in more than two months, which revived talk of Japanese intervention. Gold was near $4,044 and WTI crude was about $87.33 in the same wrap. These are intraday European prints, not closing levels.

## What to watch

With no Treasury market today, the next firm signal on rates comes when bonds reopen on Thursday. Weekly jobless claims are scheduled for Thursday, and October producer prices are tentatively scheduled for Friday; check the official BLS calendar before relying on that date.

marketImpact.summary: Overnight strength in Asian chips and firmer US futures suggest a rebound open, but the rebound rests on thin trade with no Treasury price discovery. If yields reopen higher on Thursday, the recovery in rate-sensitive technology could fade quickly.
marketImpact.timeframe: Today's open; next signal from Treasuries on Thursday, Nov. 12

tickers.rationale: Nasdaq futures pointed to a rebound after Tuesday's 0.74% Nasdaq Composite decline; the index is sensitive to the rate-hike outlook
Chip stocks rallied in Asia, but Nvidia had fallen more than 5% on Tuesday and its results are due this week
Bond market closed; the first clean price reaction to Tuesday's 4.98% 10-year close comes when Treasuries reopen

catalysts.event: Weekly jobless claims and Treasury trading resumes after the Veterans Day holiday
FOMC meeting, Dec. 8-9; markets price a quarter-point hike, with a half-point move in play
